title: the audit head signed hourly, an anchor folder the box's root can write over refused (plan 10 row 10G-2)
note: No box, share or Docker daemon here. The refusal of a write is shown on a stand-in (a read-only head and a non-root account); the cron lines are tested as text and on a temporary cron folder.

findings.claim: The root-overwrite test asks the kernel whether the newest head can be written (access(2)); it does not ask whether a head can be deleted or renamed. A share that refuses an overwrite but lets the box's root delete the newest heads widens the window a rewrite goes unseen to the oldest head left; a WORM share or chattr +a on heads/ closes it, and nothing checks for it

The refusal has not been run on a real anchor folder (the hospital's share with root squashed, a WORM share, chattr +i on a local disk): it is shown on a read-only file and a non-root account only. The first box's install shows it: an anchor on the box's own disk must make audit-sign exit 1 and doctor audit_heads say 'lets this box's root overwrite a signed head' (FAIL in PRODUCTION, WARN in VALIDATION)

doctor cannot test the anchor folders itself: check_host.sh mounts them read-only into the image, so every write is refused there. It reads the last hourly run's result (deploy/logs/audit-sign.json), so a folder that became writable is a FAIL at most one run later, not at once
